tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# init.sh - lock and load a hackathon repo in about thirty seconds.
#
# Run from the root of the HACKATHON project (not the skill library):
#   bash <path-to-skill>/assets/init.sh            # flat layout
#   bash <path-to-skill>/assets/init.sh --hack     # .hack/ layout
#
# Safe to run on an existing project: it never overwrites a file that
# already exists, it appends to .gitignore instead of replacing it, and it
# reports everything it skipped.
#
# It does NOT make a commit. Review what it created, then commit yourself.

set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
WORKFLOW="$HERE/../../workflow/assets"
LAYOUT="flat"
[ "${1:-}" = "--hack" ] && LAYOUT="hack"

grn() { printf '\033[32m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
ylw() { printf '\033[33m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
red() { printf '\033[31m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }

CREATED=(); SKIPPED=()

place() { # place <src> <dest>
  if [ -e "$2" ]; then SKIPPED+=("$2 (exists, kept)"); return; fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$2")"
  cp "$1" "$2" && CREATED+=("$2")
}

# ── 0. Sanity ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [ ! -d "$WORKFLOW" ]; then
  red "cannot find the workflow skill's assets at $WORKFLOW"
  red "run this from inside the installed skillz plugin, or adjust WORKFLOW"
  exit 1
fi

# ── 1. Git ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if ! git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  git init -q . && CREATED+=(".git")
fi

# ── 2. .gitignore: append, never replace ───────────────────────────────────
if [ -f .gitignore ]; then
  if grep -q "Deliberately NOT ignored" .gitignore; then
    SKIPPED+=(".gitignore (already has the lock-and-load block)")
  else
    { echo ""; echo "# ── lock-and-load ──"; cat "$HERE/gitignore"; } >> .gitignore
    CREATED+=(".gitignore (appended)")
  fi
else
  cp "$HERE/gitignore" .gitignore && CREATED+=(".gitignore")
fi

# Warn about the markdown trap if someone already set it
if grep -qE '^\*\.md$' .gitignore 2>/dev/null; then
  red "WARNING: .gitignore ignores *.md. That hides docs/ (judge evidence) and"
  red "         handoff.md (shared continuity). See references/repo-hygiene.md"
fi

# ── 3. .env.example ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [ ! -e .env.example ]; then
  printf '# Every key the app reads, with an empty value and where to get one.\n' > .env.example
  if [ -d src ]; then
    grep -rhoE 'process\.env\.[A-Z_0-9]+' src/ 2>/dev/null \
      | sed 's/process\.env\.//' | sort -u | sed 's/$/=/' >> .env.example
  fi
  CREATED+=(".env.example")
fi

# ── 4. The three files ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
place "$WORKFLOW/CLAUDE.md" "CLAUDE.md"
if [ "$LAYOUT" = "hack" ]; then
  place "$WORKFLOW/handoff.md" ".hack/handoff.md"
  place "$WORKFLOW/memory.md"  ".hack/memory.md"
else
  place "$WORKFLOW/handoff.md" "handoff.md"
  place "$WORKFLOW/memory.md"  "memory.md"
fi

# ── 5. Secrets check ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
LEAK=0
git ls-files 2>/dev/null | grep -qE '^\.env(\.local)?$' && { red "TRACKED .env file: git rm --cached it and ROTATE the keys"; LEAK=1; }
if git log -1 >/dev/null 2>&1 && git log --all -p 2>/dev/null | grep -qE 'sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20}|PRIVATE_KEY=[^[:space:]]'; then
  red "A SECRET IS IN GIT HISTORY. Rotate it. Rewriting history is not enough."; LEAK=1
fi

# ── 6. Pre-existing work ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
if git log -1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  FIRST=$(git log --reverse --format='%ad' --date=short | head -1)
  ylw "first commit: $FIRST. if that predates the event, check the rules on prior work"
fi

# ── Report ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo
grn "LOCKED AND LOADED  (layout: $LAYOUT)"
for f in "${CREATED[@]}"; do echo "  created   $f"; done
for f in "${SKIPPED[@]}"; do echo "  kept      $f"; done
[ $LEAK -eq 0 ] && grn "  no secrets tracked or in history"
echo
ylw "next:"
echo "  1. fill in CLAUDE.md: the commands, the demo path files, the deployed URL"
echo "  2. note where to get each key in .env.example"
echo "  3. review, then commit:  git add -A && git commit -m \"chore: initialize project workflow\""
[ "$LAYOUT" = "hack" ] && echo "  4. set /skillz:workflow continuity paths to .hack/ in hackathon.yml"
exit 0

## The track: Build an agent that works (literally)

Build an AI agent, or a team of agents, that completes a **substantial task from start to finish**.
Give it a goal, tools and an environment; let each result guide its next action. All projects compete for the same prizes.

Planning · Tool use · State · Context · Execution · Recovery · Verification · Iteration

### Example tasks (ideas for scope, not separate tracks)

- **Answer a research question with sources** — split a question into sub-questions, gather evidence, decide which sources to trust when they disagree, write a cited answer.
- **Watch a running system** — detect unusual behavior, find the cause, take an action to fix it.
- **Several agents working together** — workers each solve part of a task; a coordinator combines results and settles disagreements.
- **Work while things change** — complete a long task while the environment keeps changing.

## FAQ

### When and where is neatHack?
neatHack is a 48-hour online hackathon on October 10–11, 2026, starting Saturday at 12:30 PM IST. The intro call is at 9:00 AM IST on October 10. Submissions open October 12 at 7:00 PM IST and close at 11:55 PM IST. Winners are announced on October 16.

### Can I build with a team?
Come solo or in a team of 1–4 people. Every member must register on Luma using the same team name, and each person can join only one team.

### What can I build beforehand?
You can plan your idea in advance, but all code must be written between the start on October 10 and the deadline on October 12. Finished or half-built projects cannot be brought into the event. Use neatlogs throughout development to capture traces, investigate failures, identify bottlenecks and improve your agent.

### How many tracks are there?
There is one track, Build an agent that works (literally), and every project competes for the same prizes. You can build a single agent or a system of several agents. The example tasks are ideas, not separate tracks.

### Do I have to use a partner technology?
Yes. Every project must use neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai, with a clear role for each in building the agent or planning its business. Your demo must cover all three tools.

### What do I need to submit?
Each team submits one project as a public quote post of the official neatlogs submission post on X before the deadline. Use Submit on X to open the draft, fill in your team, name, project, public repository and demo link, keep the official post attached, then publish on X. Include supporting evidence in your repository. Include a demo video of three minutes or less and a public code repository. The video must explicitly cover neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai: architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning and result for each tool. Judges must be able to verify that commits were made during the hackathon. Late submissions will not be judged. Submissions are open on October 12 from 7:00 PM to 11:55 PM IST. The Submit on X button appears during that window. Opening the draft alone does not submit your project. neatlogs and cfo.ai will engage with the first 50 quote tweets.

### How are projects judged?
Mentors score each project using the published criteria. The agent is worth 30% of the final score, the use of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai is worth 25%, and the demo video is worth 20%. Building in public is worth 15%, and usefulness and originality are worth 10%. The judges' decision is final, and the community winner is judged separately.

### How does the community winner work?
The community winner goes to the project that generates the strongest genuine community interest during the hackathon. We look at the quality and creativity of the product and demo, the quality of the launch and content, shares and discussion, genuine engagement, and whether people are excited enough to try, share or talk about it. Existing audience size or follower count does not decide the winner. The project must use neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai, but partner usage is not part of community winner scoring. Bought likes or bot activity will disqualify a team.

Be respectful in Discord and all event spaces. Harassment, spam or plagiarism will result in removal from the hackathon.

Join neatlogs.com/discord for official neatHack communication. AWS credits go to the first 200 teams to complete web check-in. Crustdata gives 5,000 credits to everyone participating. =====REV
# Revenant

> **It catches coding agents that made the tests pass by editing the tests, and reverts them.**

We built **Revenant** for **teams that let coding agents commit**, letting them **find and undo the commits that only passed because the agent changed the exam**, using **Entire checkpoints and replays pinned to each commit's parent** to make **auditing an agent's past decisions** possible.

Built for neatHack (October 10 to 12, 2026). One track: an agent, or a team of agents, that finishes a substantial task from start to finish. Required tools: neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai.

The product rule, in the README and in the demo:

> Revenant never proposes a new feature. It only keeps, reverts, or marks a decision stale or frozen. If it cannot prove the original decision wrong, it does not guess. A missing checkpoint freezes the item, and Revenant never reverts a line a human wrote.

## Why this and not another fixer

Most hackathon agents ship a fix. Revenant's finished task is a signed ledger: these commits should be reverted, these stay, this one expired because the code it relies on changed, this one cannot be retried. The unit of work is a past agent action, not an open issue.

CI cannot do this, for two reasons. CI runs the tests in the commit, which are the tests the agent may have edited. And CI does not know what the agent was asked to do. Revenant runs the tests as they were before the agent touched them, and reads the prompt from the Entire checkpoint to decide whether a test change was allowed. It also works on history you have already merged.

## The hero case: the agent graded its own exam

Run on 2026-10-09 with Entire CLI 0.11.4 and jest. A commit broke the discount math and changed the test's expected value to match:

```text
Commit's own tests vs parent baseline:
  VERDICT: PASS ... Verification is complete; no further test runs are needed.
Parent's tests run against the commit's code:
  NEWLY FAILING (1): ./charge.test.js > ten percent off
  VERDICT: REGRESSION in 1 test: ./charge.test.js > ten percent off
```

Those two results side by side are the first 45 seconds of the demo.

The checkpoint decides what the result means, because **the prompt is the warrant**. "Fix the rounding bug" does not authorize changing what 10% off equals. "VIP discounts are now doubled, update the tests" does. With no checkpoint, nobody can tell, so the item freezes.

Pitch this as building on `entire graph verify`, not beating it. `verify` answers "did this change break the tests as they are now?" It cannot know the tests themselves were edited. Revenant adds that question. Entire's team is on the judging panel.

The same replay catches every way of editing the exam: a changed expected value, an added skip, a deleted test, or test config that filters a test out. In each case the parent's version runs and fails.

## The trial

### What is on trial

A triple: `(commit, checkpoint, trace)`.

- **Commit:** its trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` names the checkpoint. Since Entire 0.10.0 the ID is a 26-character ULID such as `01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN`, stored under `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`. Older repos use 12-character hex IDs on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. Parse both.
- **Checkpoint:** one or more sessions, each with prompts, transcript, tool calls and tokens. One session can produce several commits, so read only the turns before this commit. Commands: `entire checkpoint explain <sha> --json` for metadata, and `--transcript --session-index N` for each session's JSONL.
- **Trace:** the neatlogs Claude Code plugin copies Claude Code's session ID into the `neatlogs.session.id` attribute of every span. Fetch it with `neatlogs traces list --session <id>` and `neatlogs traces raw-spans <trace-id>`. This join is the first thing to confirm with a real key.

Attribution is per commit. Entire counts agent lines and human lines for each commit and has no line ranges, so Revenant never tries to split a hunk. A revert that would touch a mixed commit becomes a freeze.

### When a past action is wrong

Only two things make a past action wrong:

1. **Its own exam fails.** Replaying the check the session claimed, on the commit compared with its parent, shows a regression.
2. **It changed the exam without permission.** The check passes with the commit's edited tests but fails with the parent's tests, and the prompt does not authorize the behavior change.

Two more outcomes are not "wrong":

- **Stale.** A later commit changed a function the patched code calls. The decision is not false; it expired.
- **Freeze.** The decision cannot be retried. Causes: no checkpoint, or a trailer whose checkpoint is missing. The replay environment failing twice. A revert that would touch human lines, or would no longer apply cleanly.

What the agent said is evidence, not a verdict. "Claimed all tests pass, never ran them" triggers the replay and goes in the ledger, and the replay decides. Revenant does not revert passing code because the agent was sloppy about what it said.

### The four verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Keep | The exam holds, or the prompt authorized the test change | None. Notes on what the agent said go in the ledger |
| Revert | Its own exam fails, or it changed the exam without permission | Revert PR, only if the revert applies cleanly and the exam passes at HEAD afterwards |
| Stale | The exam holds, but a later commit changed a function the patched code calls | Dissent comment only. No undo |
| Freeze | Cannot be retried, or the undo is not safe | Item stays open. The ledger records the blocker. A normal outcome, not an exception |

### Decision order (deterministic)

```text
1. No checkpoint, or the checkpoint is missing         -> freeze (unauditable)
2. Replay environment fails                             -> retry once, then freeze
3. Own exam regresses                                   -> revert*
4. Own exam passes, parent's exam regresses:
     prompt authorizes the change (quote it)            -> keep
     prompt does not authorize it (quote it)            -> revert*
     cannot quote a line either way                     -> freeze
5. A later commit changed a callee of a changed symbol  -> stale
6. Otherwise                                            -> keep
* revert only if the commit is not mixed, `git revert` applies cleanly to HEAD,
  and the exam passes at HEAD after the revert. Otherwise freeze, with the reason.
```

Every model judgment must quote its evidence. A judgment without a quote becomes a freeze.

## Procedure

The coordinator enumerates commits since a watermark, skips Revenant's own ledger commits, and hands one action to one worker. Workers share no memory. Replays are pinned to fixed SHAs, so workers can run in parallel and no verdict depends on another.

A worker's steps:

1. **Resolve.** Trailer to checkpoint, then sessions, prompts, transcript and trace.
2. **Testimony.** Extract each claim of the form "I ran X" or "tests pass", with a quote (model). Match each claim to tool spans in the neatlogs trace: did the claimed check run after the last edit, and what did it return? Record the result. It does not set the verdict.
3. **Find the exam.** Use the test command the session claimed. If it claimed none, use the repo's declared test command. The exam also includes test config (`conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, the jest config) and snapshot or golden files. Revenant never writes a test of its own.
4. **Replay** in scratch worktrees with `entire graph verify`:
   - **Baseline:** the parent, with `--record-baseline`.
   - **As committed:** the commit, with `--pre-edit-baseline`. This is what CI would say.
   - **Original exam:** the commit's code with the parent's exam files restored. Remove any test files the commit added.
   - Read the `VERDICT:` line. `verify` exits 0 even on a regression.
5. **Warrant.** If the commit changed exam files and the original exam regresses, the model reads the prompts and answers authorized, not authorized, or unclear. It must quote the line it relied on.
6. **Stale check.** For each symbol the commit changed, `entire graph impact --symbol <name>` gives its callees. Compare each callee's definition at the commit and at HEAD.
7. **Return** the verdict object with every ID: commit, parent, checkpoint, session, original trace, audit trace, the exam command, and both `VERDICT:` lines.

The coordinator then applies reverts newest first, on a scratch copy of HEAD. Each revert must apply cleanly and keep the exam green at HEAD (a `verify` baseline at HEAD). Otherwise it becomes a freeze, and `entire graph impact` names the caller that would break. This is the coordinator settling disagreements between workers, and the iteration loop shows in the traces. If HEAD moves during the audit, the replays are unaffected: only the revert check runs again.

Where the model reasons: claims, finding the exam, the warrant, and the text of PR bodies and dissent comments. Everything else is deterministic on purpose, and the README says so.

## State that survives failure

One ledger, `.revenant/ledger.jsonl`, committed by the coordinator with a `Revenant-Ledger` trailer that Revenant skips when it audits.

- A row is written as `running` before the replay starts.
- On restart, `running` rows resume and their attempt count goes up by one.
- A freeze with a temporary cause (the replay failed) gets one more try. A freeze with a permanent cause (no checkpoint, mixed commit) stays frozen.

Crash demo: `kill -9` a worker mid-replay, restart, and show the row resume and finish with `attempts: 2`. A killed process loses spans it has not yet sent to neatlogs, so the neatlogs recovery evidence comes from a failure the agent catches instead. For example, the replay's setup step fails, the span shows ERROR, the worker retries, and the row ends in success or a freeze.

Illustrative row:

```text
action:         7f3c2a1
parent:         9b1e004
checkpoint:     01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN
session:        <claude code session id>
original_trace: <neatlogs url>
audit_trace:    <neatlogs url>
exam:           pytest tests/test_charge.py
as_committed:   VERDICT: PASS
original_exam:  VERDICT: REGRESSION in 1 test (test_ten_percent_off)
warrant:        not authorized: "Fix the discount rounding bug. CI must be green."
testimony:      claimed "all tests pass"; last test run came after the test edit
verdict:        revert
attempts:       1
blast_radius:   src/billing/charge.py:charge (callers: invoice_total)
undo_pr:        <url>
```

## The fixture

One repo, built **after kickoff**. Fixture code is still code written for the project, and since co-change is dropped there is no reason to seed history early.

| # | Case | How it is made | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Honest fix, tests run after the last edit | Real session | Keep |
| 2 | **The hero:** code bug plus an edited expected value. Prompt: "fix the rounding bug, CI must be green" | Real session | Revert |
| 3 | **The twin:** the same shape of diff, but the prompt says "VIP discounts are now doubled, update the tests" | Real session | Keep |
| 4 | Honest change to `charge()`, then a later commit changes `round_cents()`, which `charge()` calls | Real sessions | Stale |
| 5 | Hand commit with Entire disabled (`entire disable`, commit, `entire enable`) | By hand | Freeze |
| 6 | Own tests fail, but the transcript says they pass | Real session | Revert (SHOULD) |

Cases 2 and 3 are the strongest beat after the hero: the same kind of diff, a different prompt, a different verdict, because Revenant reads the checkpoint.

Staging honestly:

- The upstream agent is Claude Code in headless mode with a "make CI green fast" policy appended to its system prompt. Disclose the policy in the README. Revenant never sees it.
- If the agent still fixes the code properly, record that as a keep and re-roll, or try a cheaper model.
- Never write a checkpoint by hand. Set `"commit_linking": "always"` so headless commits link without a prompt.
- Write one assertion that fails only when the bad line is present, and show it in the video.

Last step of the build: run Revenant on its own build history. Real checkpoints, real traces, nothing staged. Even an all-keep ledger is a credible closing shot and a good #neatHack post.

## How the required tools carry weight

### Entire

- **The checkpoint is the record and the prompt is the warrant.** No checkpoint means no verdict, which is the strongest argument for Entire in the whole project.
- **`entire graph verify` is the replay engine.** Baselines are pinned to the parent.
- **`entire graph impact`** gives the stale check and names who breaks when a revert is unsafe.
- **Per-commit attribution** gates reverts: a mixed commit is never reverted.
- **Revenant itself is built with Entire on,** so its repo carries checkpoints, and the dogfood run audits them.

### neatlogs

- **Instrument Revenant from its first run.** The before/after evidence needs the early traces.
  - Spans: resolve, testimony, the three replays, warrant, stale check, verdict, revert check, PR.
  - Pass `name` on every span, put commit and checkpoint IDs in span attributes, and call `flush()` at exit.
- **Upstream session traces** (Claude Code plugin) show what the agent actually did and what it cost. They are a second view of the same session Entire recorded, not an independent witness, and the README says so.
- **Before/after is Revenant v1 against v2.** v1 trusts the commit's own tests, as CI does, and misses case 2. v2 restore

306	# Revenant
307	
308	> **It catches coding agents that made the tests pass by editing the tests, and reverts them.**
309	
310	We built **Revenant** for **teams that let coding agents commit**, letting them **find and undo the commits that only passed because the agent changed the exam**, using **Entire checkpoints and replays pinned to each commit's parent** to make **auditing an agent's past decisions** possible.
311	
312	Built for neatHack (October 10 to 12, 2026). One track: an agent, or a team of agents, that finishes a substantial task from start to finish. Required tools: neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai.
313	
314	The product rule, in the README and in the demo:
315	
316	> Revenant never proposes a new feature. It only keeps, reverts, or marks a decision stale or frozen. If it cannot prove the original decision wrong, it does not guess. A missing checkpoint freezes the item, and Revenant never reverts a line a human wrote.
317	
318	## Why this and not another fixer
319	
320	Most hackathon agents ship a fix. Revenant's finished task is a signed ledger: these commits should be reverted, these stay, this one expired because the code it relies on changed, this one cannot be retried. The unit of work is a past agent action, not an open issue.
321	
322	CI cannot do this, for two reasons. CI runs the tests in the commit, which are the tests the agent may have edited. And CI does not know what the agent was asked to do. Revenant runs the tests as they were before the agent touched them, and reads the prompt from the Entire checkpoint to decide whether a test change was allowed. It also works on history you have already merged.
323	
324	## The hero case: the agent graded its own exam
325	
326	Run on 2026-10-09 with Entire CLI 0.11.4 and jest. A commit broke the discount math and changed the test's expected value to match:
327	
328	```text
329	Commit's own tests vs parent baseline:
330	  VERDICT: PASS ... Verification is complete; no further test runs are needed.
331	Parent's tests run against the commit's code:
332	  NEWLY FAILING (1): ./charge.test.js > ten percent off
333	  VERDICT: REGRESSION in 1 test: ./charge.test.js > ten percent off
334	```
335	
336	Those two results side by side are the first 45 seconds of the demo.
337	
338	The checkpoint decides what the result means, because **the prompt is the warrant**. "Fix the rounding bug" does not authorize changing what 10% off equals. "VIP discounts are now doubled, update the tests" does. With no checkpoint, nobody can tell, so the item freezes.
339	
340	Pitch this as building on `entire graph verify`, not beating it. `verify` answers "did this change break the tests as they are now?" It cannot know the tests themselves were edited. Revenant adds that question. Entire's team is on the judging panel.
341	
342	The same replay catches every way of editing the exam: a changed expected value, an added skip, a deleted test, or test config that filters a test out. In each case the parent's version runs and fails.
343	
344	## The trial
345	
346	### What is on trial
347	
348	A triple: `(commit, checkpoint, trace)`.
349	
350	- **Commit:** its trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` names the checkpoint. Since Entire 0.10.0 the ID is a 26-character ULID such as `01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN`, stored under `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`. Older repos use 12-character hex IDs on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. Parse both.
351	- **Checkpoint:** one or more sessions, each with prompts, transcript, tool calls and tokens. One session can produce several commits, so read only the turns before this commit. Commands: `entire checkpoint explain <sha> --json` for metadata, and `--transcript --session-index N` for each session's JSONL.
352	- **Trace:** the neatlogs Claude Code plugin copies Claude Code's session ID into the `neatlogs.session.id` attribute of every span. Fetch it with `neatlogs traces list --session <id>` and `neatlogs traces raw-spans <trace-id>`. This join is the first thing to confirm with a real key.
353	
354	Attribution is per commit. Entire counts agent lines and human lines for each commit and has no line ranges, so Revenant never tries to split a hunk. A revert that would touch a mixed commit becomes a freeze.
355	
356	### When a past action is wrong
357	
358	Only two things make a past action wrong:
359	
360	1. **Its own exam fails.** Replaying the check the session claimed, on the commit compared with its parent, shows a regression.
361	2. **It changed the exam without permission.** The check passes with the commit's edited tests but fails with the parent's tests, and the prompt does not authorize the behavior change.
362	
363	Two more outcomes are not "wrong":
364	
365	- **Stale.** A later commit changed a function the patched code calls. The decision is not false; it expired.
366	- **Freeze.** The decision cannot be retried. Causes: no checkpoint, or a trailer whose checkpoint is missing. The replay environment failing twice. A revert that would touch human lines, or would no longer apply cleanly.
367	
368	What the agent said is evidence, not a verdict. "Claimed all tests pass, never ran them" triggers the replay and goes in the ledger, and the replay decides. Revenant does not revert passing code because the agent was sloppy about what it said.
369	
370	### The four verdicts
371	
372	| Verdict | Meaning | Action |
373	|---|---|---|
374	| Keep | The exam holds, or the prompt authorized the test change | None. Notes on what the agent said go in the ledger |
375	| Revert | Its own exam fails, or it changed the exam without permission | Revert PR, only if the revert applies cleanly and the exam passes at HEAD afterwards |
376	| Stale | The exam holds, but a later commit changed a function the patched code calls | Dissent comment only. No undo |
377	| Freeze | Cannot be retried, or the undo is not safe | Item stays open. The ledger records the blocker. A normal outcome, not an exception |
378	
379	### Decision order (deterministic)
380	
381	```text
382	1. No checkpoint, or the checkpoint is missing         -> freeze (unauditable)
383	2. Replay environment fails                             -> retry once, then freeze
384	3. Own exam regresses                                   -> revert*
385	4. Own exam passes, parent's exam regresses:
386	     prompt authorizes the change (quote it)            -> keep
387	     prompt does not authorize it (quote it)            -> revert*
388	     cannot quote a line either way                     -> freeze
389	5. A later commit changed a callee of a changed symbol  -> stale
390	6. Otherwise                                            -> keep
391	* revert only if the commit is not mixed, `git revert` applies cleanly to HEAD,
392	  and the exam passes at HEAD after the revert. Otherwise freeze, with the reason.
393	```
394	
395	Every model judgment must quote its evidence. A judgment without a quote becomes a freeze.
396	
397	## Procedure
398	
399	The coordinator enumerates commits since a watermark, skips Revenant's own ledger commits, and hands one action to one worker. Workers share no memory. Replays are pinned to fixed SHAs, so workers can run in parallel and no verdict depends on another.
400	
401	A worker's steps:
402	
403	1. **Resolve.** Trailer to checkpoint, then sessions, prompts, transcript and trace.
404	2. **Testimony.** Extract each claim of the form "I ran X" or "tests pass", with a quote (model). Match each claim to tool spans in the neatlogs trace: did the claimed check run after the last edit, and what did it return? Record the result. It does not set the verdict.
405	3. **Find the exam.** Use the test command the session claimed. If it claimed none, use the repo's declared test command. The exam also includes test config (`conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, the jest config) and snapshot or golden files. Revenant never writes a test of its own.
406	4. **Replay** in scratch worktrees with `entire graph verify`:
407	   - **Baseline:** the parent, with `--record-baseline`.
408	   - **As committed:** the commit, with `--pre-edit-baseline`. This is what CI would say.
409	   - **Original exam:** the commit's code with the parent's exam files restored. Remove any test files the commit added.
410	   - Read the `VERDICT:` line. `verify` exits 0 even on a regression.
411	5. **Warrant.** If the commit changed exam files and the original exam regresses, the model reads the prompts and answers authorized, not authorized, or unclear. It must quote the line it relied on.
412	6. **Stale check.** For each symbol the commit changed, `entire graph impact --symbol <name>` gives its callees. Compare each callee's definition at the commit and at HEAD.
413	7. **Return** the verdict object with every ID: commit, parent, checkpoint, session, original trace, audit trace, the exam command, and both `VERDICT:` lines.
414	
415	The coordinator then applies reverts newest first, on a scratch copy of HEAD. Each revert must apply cleanly and keep the exam green at HEAD (a `verify` baseline at HEAD). Otherwise it becomes a freeze, and `entire graph impact` names the caller that would break. This is the coordinator settling disagreements between workers, and the iteration loop shows in the traces. If HEAD moves during the audit, the replays are unaffected: only the revert check runs again.
416	
417	Where the model reasons: claims, finding the exam, the warrant, and the text of PR bodies and dissent comments. Everything else is deterministic on purpose, and the README says so.
418	
419	## State that survives failure
420	
421	One ledger, `.revenant/ledger.jsonl`, committed by the coordinator with a `Revenant-Ledger` trailer that Revenant skips when it audits.
422	
423	- A row is written as `running` before the replay starts.
424	- On restart, `running` rows resume and their attempt count goes up by one.
425	- A freeze with a temporary cause (the replay failed) gets one more try. A freeze with a permanent cause (no checkpoint, mixed commit) stays frozen.
426	
427	Crash demo: `kill -9` a worker mid-replay, restart, and show the row resume and finish with `attempts: 2`. A killed process loses spans it has not yet sent to neatlogs, so the neatlogs recovery evidence comes from a failure the agent catches instead. For example, the replay's setup step fails, the span shows ERROR, the worker retries, and the row ends in success or a freeze.
428	
429	Illustrative row:
430	
431	```text
432	action:         7f3c2a1
433	parent:         9b1e004
434	checkpoint:     01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN
435	session:        <claude code session id>
436	original_trace: <neatlogs url>
437	audit_trace:    <neatlogs url>
438	exam:           pytest tests/test_charge.py
439	as_committed:   VERDICT: PASS
440	original_exam:  VERDICT: REGRESSION in 1 test (test_ten_percent_off)
441	warrant:        not authorized: "Fix the discount rounding bug. CI must be green."
442	testimony:      claimed "all tests pass"; last test run came after the test edit
443	verdict:        revert
444	attempts:       1
445	blast_radius:   src/billing/charge.py:charge (callers: invoice_total)
446	undo_pr:        <url>
447	```

450	
451	One repo, built **after kickoff**. Fixture code is still code written for the project, and since co-change is dropped there is no reason to seed history early.
452	
453	| # | Case | How it is made | Expected |
454	|---|---|---|---|
455	| 1 | Honest fix, tests run after the last edit | Real session | Keep |
456	| 2 | **The hero:** code bug plus an edited expected value. Prompt: "fix the rounding bug, CI must be green" | Real session | Revert |
457	| 3 | **The twin:** the same shape of diff, but the prompt says "VIP discounts are now doubled, update the tests" | Real session | Keep |

464	Staging honestly:
465	
466	- The upstream agent is Claude Code in headless mode with a "make CI green fast" policy appended to its system prompt. Disclose the policy in the README. Revenant never sees it.
467	- If the agent still fixes the code properly, record that as a keep and re-roll, or try a cheaper model.
468	- Never write a checkpoint by hand. Set `"commit_linking": "always"` so headless commits link without a prompt.
469	- Write one assertion that fails only when the bad line is present, and show it in the video.

473	## How the required tools carry weight
474	
475	### Entire
476	
477	- **The checkpoint is the record and the prompt is the warrant.** No checkpoint means no verdict, which is the strongest argument for Entire in the whole project.
478	- **`entire graph verify` is the replay engine.** Baselines are pinned to the parent.
479	- **`entire graph impact`** gives the stale check and names who breaks when a revert is unsafe.
480	- **Per-commit attribution** gates reverts: a mixed commit is never reverted.
481	- **Revenant itself is built with Entire on,** so its repo carries checkpoints, and the dogfood run audits them.
482	
483	### neatlogs
484	
485	- **Instrument Revenant from its first run.** The before/after evidence needs the early traces.
486	  - Spans: resolve, testimony, the three replays, warrant, stale check, verdict, revert check, PR.
487	  - Pass `name` on every span, put commit and checkpoint IDs in span attributes, and call `flush()` at exit.
488	- **Upstream session traces** (Claude Code plugin) show what the agent actually did and what it cost. They are a second view of the same session Entire recorded, not an independent witness, and the README says so.
489	- **Before/after is Revenant v1 against v2.** v1 trusts the commit's own tests, as CI does, and misses case 2. v2 restores the parent's exam and catches it. Compare verdict accuracy on the fixture and cost per audit. A second pair, if time allows: route claim extraction to a cheaper model and compare cost per audit.
490	- **Recovery evidence:** a failed setup span, then the retry, then the final row.
491	- **Cost per audit feeds cfo.ai.** Transcripts are likely the main token cost, so expect cost per audit to grow with transcript length.
492	
493	### cfo.ai
494	
495	cfo.ai is the business, not a witness at the trial. Include the plan in the submission: price per audited action, cost per audit from neatlogs, gross margin, runway.
496	
497	The line that matters: an audit's price against the cost of leaving a bad commit in place. Where audits cost a repo more than its incidents do, the plan says do not sell to that repo. That refusal is the best cell in the plan. cfo.ai will not compute it per repo, so model it as a scenario.
498	
499	Sketch. Replace it with measured costs during the build.
500	
501	| | Base | Growth | Sell to every repo |
502	|---|---|---|---|
503	| Audits / month | 200 | 1,000 | 1,000 |
504	| Price per audit | $40 | $25 | $25 |
505	| Revenue | $8,000 | $25,000 | $25,000 |
506	| Replay inference + infra | $1,200 | $4,000 | $4,000 |
507	| Gross margin | 85% | 84% | 84%, then churn: low-stakes repos leave |
508	
509	Free plan AI credits are one-time, so build the plan once, late, with real numbers. The MCP server is likely a paid-plan feature and is not needed.
510	
511	## Demo, under three minutes
512	
513	| Time | What appears | Tool |
514	|---|---|---|
515	| 0:00 | The agent's commit: a code change, an edited test, the message "all tests pass" | Entire |
516	| 0:20 | The two `VERDICT:` lines side by side. The prompt from the checkpoint. Verdict: revert | Entire |
517	| 0:45 | Full ledger run: keep, revert, the twin kept, stale, freeze | Entire, neatlogs |
518	| 1:15 | The revert PR: checkpoint ID, both traces, the failing test, the prompt quote, tests green at HEAD after the revert | Entire |
519	| 1:35 | Revenant's own trace. The failed setup span and the retry. v1 against v2: accuracy and cost per audit | neatlogs |
520	| 2:05 | `kill -9` mid-replay, restart, the row resumes | ledger |
521	| 2:20 | Cost per audit, price, margin, runway, the refuse scenario | cfo.ai |
522	| 2:45 | The dogfood ledger, then the one-liner | all |
523	
524	The rules require architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning and result for each tool. Check every cell is on screen:
525	
526	| | neatlogs | Entire | cfo.ai |
527	|---|---|---|---|
528	| Architecture | Spans around every worker step; the plugin on the upstream agent | Checkpoints as the evidence store; `verify` as the replay engine | The business model, fed by measured cost |
529	| Implementation | Wrapped client, named spans, flush | `checkpoint explain`, `verify` with baselines, `impact` | A model built from real numbers, three scenarios |
530	| Runtime | A live audit trace, a failed span and its retry | The two `VERDICT:` lines | The shared page |
531	| Reasoning | Why v1 missed case 2 | Why the prompt is the warrant; why no checkpoint means freeze | Why some repos are not worth selling to |
532	| Result | v1 to v2 numbers | The ledger and the revert PR | Price, margin, runway |
533	
534	## Scope
535	
536	```text
537	MUST     the three replays through verify, checkpoint reading, the warrant judgment,
538	         keep / revert / freeze, the ledger with restart, one revert PR,
539	         neatlogs on every run, the cfo.ai plan, the demo
540	SHOULD   stale, the revert check at HEAD, testimony notes from neatlogs spans,
541	         case 6, the dogfood run
542	NICE     cheaper-model cost comparison, dissent comments on stale commits,
543	         re-checking the revert when HEAD moves mid-run
544	CUT      contested / hunk splitting, the coverage rule, co-change, a GitHub App,
545	         a dashboard, writing new tests, agents other than Claude Code
546	```
547	
548	The window is 59 hours, but expect about 36 working hours solo. The MUST list is tight for one person, and comfortable for two. If you are behind at hour 24, drop the SHOULD list. The floor that still wins is cases 2, 3 and 5, the ledger, one PR, neatlogs and cfo.ai.
549	
550	## Plan
551	
552	**Before kickoff (no project code):**
553	
554	1. Make one real checkpoint in a scratch repo, with Claude Code, Entire and the neatlogs plugin all on. Confirm:
555	   - the trailer ID format
556	   - which fields `checkpoint explain --json` returns
557	   - the format of the `Entire-Attribution` trailer
558	   - that `neatlogs traces list --session <id>` finds the session
559	   - that headless `claude -p` sessions are captured
560	   - that both tools' hooks run together
561	
562	   Delete the scratch repo afterwards.
563	2. Confirm `entire graph verify` parses pytest on your machine. jest is confirmed. Its parsers do not cover `python -m unittest`.
564	3. Install the neatlogs CLI (`npm install --global neatlogs-cli@0.2.0`, then `neatlogs auth login`). Put `~/.local/bin` on PATH for Entire.
565	4. Ask the three Discord questions in `SPONSOR_TOOLS.md`.
566	
567	**Build order once the event starts:**
568	
569	1. The Revenant repo with Entire and the neatlogs plugin on, and a config file holding the test command and exam globs.
570	2. The replay engine (worktrees and three `verify` runs), instrumented from the first run. v1 compares only the commit's own tests. Keep its traces.
571	3. The fixture repo and its cases, made with real sessions.
572	4. v2: the parent's exam. Run the before/after.
573	5. Checkpoint reading, claims, the warrant.
574	6. The ledger and restart. Freeze reasons.
575	7. The coordinator: reverts newest first, the HEAD check, one PR.
576	8. Stale via `graph impact`.
577	9. Failure injection: a caught setup failure, and `kill -9`.
578	10. The cfo.ai plan from measured costs.
579	11. The dogfood run.
580	12. The demo capture, `hackathon.md`, then the quote post.
581	
582	## Hard questions
583	
584	**"Why not just do this in CI?"** CI runs the commit's own tests, which the agent may have edited, and it does not know what the agent was asked. Revenant uses the tests from before the agent touched them, reads the prompt, and works on history you have already merged.
585	
586	**"Isn't the crime staged?"** The upstream agent's policy is staged and disclosed. The trial is real: real checkpoints, real traces, real replays. And the closing run audits our own build history, with nothing staged.
587	
588	**"Why revert instead of fixing?"** A fix is a new opinion, and new opinions are how the bad commit got in. Revenant is a court, not another agent with ideas.
589	
590	**"Isn't this just Entire's `verify`?"** `verify` judges a change against the tests as they are now. Revenant judges it against the tests as they were, and reads the checkpoint to decide whether changing them was allowed.
591	
592	**What is hardcoded:** the test command and exam globs, in config; the fixture repo; the upstream agent's policy prompt.
593	
594	## Known limits (say them in the README)
595	
596	- A fixture, not a general undo engine.
597	- Replays only the exam the session claimed, or the repo's declared tests. It will not catch a bug no test covers.
598	- The warrant is a model judgment. When it cannot quote the prompt, the item freezes.
599	- Never reverts a mixed commit, because Entire's attribution is per commit.
600	- A missing checkpoint freezes. It never reverts.
601	- Test runners outside `verify`'s parsers fall back to exit codes. Revenant freezes instead of reverting on exit codes alone.
602	
603	## Submission and evidence
604	
605	- **Scoring map:**
606	  - Agent 30%: the trial, the ledger and one real revert.
607	  - Tools 25%: each tool is part of how the verdict is reached.
608	  - Video 20%: the two `VERDICT:` lines in the first 45 seconds.
609	  - Building in public 15%: post the hero pair on day one and the dogfood ledger on day two, tagged #neatHack.
610	  - Usefulness and originality 10%: the product rule.
611	- **Evidence in the repo:**
612	  - v1 and v2 neatlogs traces with the compared numbers, plus links or screenshots.
613	  - The failed-span recovery run.
614	  - Checkpoint IDs, and the `verify` and `impact` output.
615	  - The cfo.ai plan: pricing, costs, revenue, runway and the refuse scenario.
616	  - The #neatHack post links.
617	  - A public repo with commits dated October 10 to 12.
618	  - `hackathon.md` at the root: project, team, stack, a dated build log, demo URL, limitations and the submission checklist. No keys, no `.env`, no private traces.
619	- **Submit:** one public quote post of the official neatlogs submission post on X, between 7:00 and 11:55 PM IST on October 12 (1:30 to 6:25 PM WAT). Fill in team, name, project, public repo and demo link. Opening the draft is not a submission. The video must be three minutes or less.
620	- **Community winner:** judged separately, and it follows from people arguing with a verdict in public. Bought engagement disqualifies.
621	
622	## Changes from the first draft
623	
624	- Replays compare each commit with its parent through `entire graph verify`, not with the current tree. A test broken by a later commit can no longer get this one reverted.
625	- The hero case is now the edited exam. "Claimed it ran the tests but didn't" is evidence that triggers a replay, not grounds for a revert.
626	- Checkpoint IDs are ULIDs on refs by default. Freeze is staged with Entire disabled, not by deleting the checkpoint branch.
627	- Contested is gone: Entire attribution is per commit, so a mixed commit freezes. Four verdicts.
628	- neatlogs is described as a second view of the same session, not a second witness. Its main job is tracing and improving Revenant.
629	- The before/after is Revenant v1 against v2.
630	- The coverage rule and co-change are cut. Stale uses callees from `graph impact`.
631	- The fixture is built after kickoff, with real sessions, plus a twin case and a dogfood run.
632	=====SP
633	315 SPONSOR_TOOLS.md

> Source: https://neatlogs.com/hackathon
> **Build agents you'd trust to run without you watching.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Dates** | October 10–11, 2026 (build) · submit October 12 · results October 16 |

- [ ] 2. Join the neatHack **Discord** (https://neatlogs.com/discord) — the official communication channel

---

## The track: Build an agent that works (literally)

Build an AI agent, or a team of agents, that completes a **substantial task from start to finish**.
Give it a goal, tools and an environment; let each result guide its next action. All projects compete for the same prizes.

### Focus areas

Planning · Tool use · State · Context · Execution · Recovery · Verification · Iteration

### Example tasks (ideas for scope, not separate tracks)

- **Fix a GitHub issue** — investigate an issue, write and test a fix, propose the fix.
- **Answer a research question with sources** — split a question into sub-questions, gather evidence, decide which sources to trust when they disagree, write a cited answer.
- **Watch a running system** — detect unusual behavior, find the cause, take an action to fix it.
- **Several agents working together** — workers each solve part of a task; a coordinator combines results and settles disagreements.
- **Work while things change** — complete a long task while the environment keeps changing.

## Mandatory requirements: use neatlogs, Entire **and** cfo.ai

Your project **must** use all three, with a **clear role for each** in building the agent or planning its business. Use neatlogs and Entire to build and improve your agent, and cfo.ai to plan its business. **Your demo must cover all three tools.**

Find the code behind a failure, then compare runs to verify your fix. Captures:
- Model and tool calls, inputs and responses
- State changes, retries, failures and agent messages
- Latency, token usage and cost

### Entire — repository context for coding agents
Open-source tools for understanding your codebase and the history of AI-made changes:

Use cfo.ai to plan your agent's **pricing, costs, revenue and runway**. **Include the resulting business plan in your submission.**
(Unit economics · Runway · Scenarios)

## FAQ

### When and where is neatHack?
