# Revenant

Revenant catches commits where a coding agent got the tests to pass by editing the tests, then reverts those commits. It is for teams that let coding agents commit.

Hackathon: neatHack. Submission window: Oct 12, 7:00 to 11:55 PM IST (15:30 to 20:25 CEST).
Feature freeze: **Oct 12, 4:00 PM IST (12:30 CEST)**. After that, only fixes, the demo video, the README and evidence.

The full design lives in `../REVENANT.md` (outside the repo). The durable parts are in `memory.md`.

## Before starting work

Read `handoff.md` first, then check it against the repo (`git log --oneline -5`,
`git status --porcelain`). If they disagree, trust the repo. `memory.md` holds the
durable project knowledge, so check it before rediscovering anything.

## The product rule (never violate)

Revenant never proposes a new feature. It only keeps, reverts, or marks a decision stale
or frozen. If it cannot prove the original decision wrong, it does not guess. A missing
checkpoint freezes the item. A mixed human and agent commit is never reverted. A model
judgment that does not quote its evidence becomes a freeze.

## Commands

TypeScript run directly by Node 22 (no build step). Architecture: `docs/architecture-brief.md`.

```bash
npm run typecheck                            # cheapest useful check, before every commit
node src/cli.ts replay <sha>... --repo <path> [--json]   # exam from <path>/revenant.config.json
git push || git push                         # first push after a new checkpoint fails, see memory.md

# replay engine (verify exits 0 even on a regression: read the VERDICT: line)
entire graph verify --record-baseline        # at the parent
entire graph verify --pre-edit-baseline      # at the commit
entire graph impact --symbol <name>          # callees, for stale and blast radius
entire checkpoint explain <sha> --json       # checkpoint metadata
entire checkpoint explain <sha> --transcript --session-index N
neatlogs traces list --session <claude-session-id>
neatlogs traces raw-spans <trace-id>
```

No deployed URL is required. The demo is the CLI and the ledger, recorded on video.

## The demo path

These files are what gets judged. Verify changes to them with a real run on the fixture, not just a green build:

```text
src/replay.ts           verify runs in scratch worktrees (.revenant/worktrees/), retry once
src/decide.ts           the decision table. v1 today; v2 adds the parent's exam
src/seams/entire.ts     verify wrapper + VERDICT parser (exit code is always 0)
src/seams/trace.ts      neatlogs spans: every step named, ids in attributes AND input
src/cli.ts              entry point
not yet                 worker (resolve, warrant), coordinator, ledger
```

## Sponsor tools are evidence, keep them on

- **Entire** is on for every session. Its `Entire-Checkpoint` and `Entire-Attribution`
  trailers are judged evidence and the dogfood run audits them. Never strip them, and
  never run `entire disable` in this repo. Do that only in the fixture repo, for case 5.
- **neatlogs**: give every span a `name`, put the commit and checkpoint IDs in span
  attributes, and call `flush()` at exit. Keep the v1 traces, because the before/after
  comparison needs them.

## Working stance

Slow, steady, sharp. Take the time to understand; do not spend time on work that does
not change the outcome.

- **Inspect before modifying.** Find the file, understand it, check its callers, then
  make the smallest change that works.
- **Preserve what works.** Ugly and running beats clean and broken.
- **Verify before reporting.** Run the cheapest check first, then a targeted test, then a
  real run on the fixture. Never say a change works without having checked it.
- **One change at a time when debugging.** Observe, locate, form a hypothesis, change one
  thing, verify.
- **Stop after two failed attempts.** Write it in `handoff.md` under Do not repeat and move on.
- **Protect the scope.** Before any code, sort a new idea into MUST, SHOULD, NICE or CUT,
  using the lists in `memory.md`. If behind at hour 24, drop SHOULD.

## Communication

Plain language: Found, Changed, Verified, Next. Keep the length proportional to the change.

## Before ending a session

Verify, commit, then update `handoff.md` with the exact stopping point and the one next
step. Update it at every checkpoint, not only at session end. Someone who was not here
should be able to start in under two minutes.

## Never

- Commit a secret, a `.env` file, or a private neatlogs trace export.
- Add a `Co-Authored-By` naming a tool, a generated-by footer, or a robot emoji. Entire's
  own trailers are different. They stay.
- Use em dashes in the README, docs, commit messages or comments.
- Write a checkpoint by hand, or write a test for the code under audit.
- Commit `.revenant/worktrees/`.
- Refactor after hour 20 (Oct 11, 8:30 AM IST).

# Project memory

## What this is

Revenant catches commits where a coding agent got the tests to pass by editing the tests,
then reverts those commits. It replays each commit against its parent's tests through
`entire graph verify`. It reads the prompt from the commit's Entire checkpoint to decide
whether the test change was allowed. Its output is a ledger: keep, revert, stale or
freeze. Source design: `../REVENANT.md`.

## Stack

```text
language / runner   TypeScript on Node 22 CLI; jest for the fixture. See docs/architecture-brief.md
neatlogs read CLI   needs --host https://app.neatlogs.com and NEATLOGS_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/neatlogs-cli
                    (the Claude Code plugin owns ~/.config/neatlogs/config.json in another format;
                    the CLI rejects it as UNSAFE_CONFIG_FILE). The ingest key cannot read traces,
                    and NEATLOGS_API_KEY in env OVERRIDES the OAuth login: run the CLI with
                    `env -u NEATLOGS_API_KEY ... --project 6501ac4a-c89a-4644-87e3-731a7c07a3d9`
repo                https://github.com/mikemoulder/revenant (public). Entire pushes checkpoint refs on push
Entire CLI          0.11.4, ~/.local/bin/entire. commit_linking: always (.entire/settings.json)
neatlogs CLI        0.2.0. Claude Code plugin set up globally (~/.claude/settings.json)
host                none needed. CLI plus a committed ledger; GitHub for the revert PR
```

## Architecture

The coordinator lists the commits since a watermark and skips Revenant's own ledger commits. It hands
one commit to each worker. Workers share no memory, and every replay is pinned to fixed SHAs,
so workers run in parallel. The coordinator applies reverts newest first on a scratch
copy of HEAD.

```text
commit -> trailer -> checkpoint -> sessions/prompts -> neatlogs trace (session id join)
       -> replays: parent baseline | as committed | commit code + parent's exam
       -> warrant (model, must quote) -> stale (graph impact) -> verdict -> ledger row
```

## Decisions

```text
Four verdicts: keep, revert, stale, freeze. No "contested"
  why:        Entire attribution is per commit, with no line ranges, so a mixed commit freezes
  instead of: hunk splitting (cut)

Replays compare commit vs parent, never vs current tree
  why:        a later commit's breakage must not get this one reverted

The prompt is the warrant
  why:        same diff, different prompt, different verdict (fixture cases 2 vs 3)

Agent testimony is evidence, not a verdict
  why:        a sloppy claim triggers a replay; only the replay decides

Before/after = Revenant v1 (trusts commit's own tests, misses case 2) vs v2 (parent's exam)
  instead of: comparing upstream agent runs

Freeze is a normal outcome, not an exception
```

Decision order (deterministic):
1. No checkpoint: freeze.
2. Replay env fails: retry once, then freeze.
3. Own exam regresses: revert*.
4. Own exam passes but the parent's exam regresses: authorized means keep, not authorized
   means revert*, and no quote means freeze.
5. A later commit changed a callee: stale.
6. Otherwise keep.

\* Revert only if the commit is not mixed, the revert applies cleanly, and the exam is green at HEAD afterwards. Otherwise freeze.

## Scope

```text
MUST    3 replays via verify, checkpoint reading, warrant, keep/revert/freeze,
        ledger with restart, one revert PR, neatlogs on every run, cfo.ai plan, demo
SHOULD  stale, revert check at HEAD, testimony from neatlogs spans, case 6, dogfood run
NICE    cheaper-model cost comparison, dissent comments, re-check when HEAD moves
CUT     hunk splitting, coverage rule, co-change, GitHub App, dashboard, writing tests,
        agents other than Claude Code
Floor:  cases 2, 3, 5, the ledger, one PR, neatlogs, cfo.ai
```

## Constraints

```text
All code written Oct 10 to 12        no pre-existing code; fixture repo built after kickoff
Demo video <= 3 min                  must cover arch/impl/runtime/reasoning/result per tool
Public repo                          no remote yet; must be public before submission
verify exits 0 on regression         parse the VERDICT: line, never the exit code
Unknown runner                       freeze, never revert on exit codes alone
kill -9 loses unsent spans           neatlogs recovery evidence comes from a caught failure
cfo.ai free AI credits are one-time  build the plan once, late, with measured costs
```

## Lessons

```text
Entire's files_touched only lists files edited by Write/Edit    shell-written files are absent
  (commit 05a4624: .env.example missing)                      so fixture sessions edit with Write/Edit,
                                                               and attribution may read as mixed
neatlogs join CONFIRMED: `traces list --session <claude id>`    one trace per user prompt, not per session.
  returns traces with sessionId = Entire's session_id         pick the trace whose [startedAt, completedAt]
                                                               holds the commit time (05a4624 -> 8bafa749)
Push of a commit with a NEW checkpoint fails: "main -> main    Entire's pre-push hook pushes the checkpoint ref
  (failed)". Seen on 05a4624 and f363a59                      fine, main is rejected. Second push succeeds.
                                                               Always: `git push || git push`
verify --setup "<cmd>" that FAILS is ignored;                   Revenant runs setup itself (src/replay.ts),
  verify runs the tests anyway                                 so the failure is a real ERROR span + retry
verify wording: PASS | NO EFFECT | REGRESSION in N |           "(exit N)" forms are exit-code only -> unknown.
  PASS (exit 0) | FAIL (exit N)                                an unchanged suite says NO EFFECT, not PASS
Headless `claude -p` commits DO get checkpoints (fixture 2a6d0a0)  the fixture can be built headless
  and neatlogs finds the trace by session id                   transcript JSONL line 1 holds the prompt
No Entire-Attribution trailer on commits (0.11.4)              mixed-commit check uses `entire blame <file>`
                                                               tags per line: [HU] [AI] [MX]
neatlogs session cost ($0.004) != claude -p cost ($0.079)      quote neither as truth until understood
Headless Claude adds its own Co-Authored-By trailer            fine in the fixture; it is the agent's own habit
neatlogs public API (raw-spans) omits span attributes           ids are duplicated into span input
neatlogs SDK logs INFO to stdout, level read at import          NEATLOGS_LOG_LEVEL=WARN before dynamic import
```

## What is real, what is staged

**Real:** checkpoints, traces, replays, verdicts, the revert PR, the dogfood run.
**Staged and disclosed:** the upstream agent's "make CI green fast" policy prompt, the
fixture repo, and the test command and exam globs in config.

content.text:
## What we're building, in plain terms

**The setup.** Companies now let AI coding agents like Claude Code write code and commit it themselves. Every project has **tests**, small checks such as "charging $100 with 10% off should give $90". On every commit an automatic system (CI) runs the tests. Green means "looks fine".

**The hole.** An agent can change the code **and the tests in the same commit**. If it changes a test's expected answer, CI goes green, but that proves nothing, because the agent wrote both the answers and the answer key. Sometimes that's legitimate, because the job was to change the behaviour. Sometimes it isn't. CI can't tell which, and a human reviewer often can't either, because they don't know what the agent was asked to do.

**Revenant is an auditor for agent commits.** For each past commit it:
1. **Pulls out the original answer key.** It re-runs the tests *as they were before the agent touched them* against the agent's new code. If they fail, the agent changed what the code does, even though CI was green.
2. **Looks up the assignment.** Entire saved the prompt the agent was given, alongside the commit.
3. **Rules on it:**
   - The change was asked for → **keep**, quoting the line that allowed it.
   - The commit broke its own tests → **revert**, by opening a PR that undoes it.
   - There's no record, so it can't be judged → **freeze**, flag it and touch nothing.
4. **Writes it all to a ledger**, with the evidence.

**A real example from today.** In commit `87930b6`, an agent asked to fix a rounding bug also changed a VIP price test from $3.91 to $3.92. CI was green. Revenant runs the *old* test and gets a failure, so it knows the VIP price changed. Then it reads the prompt: "half-cent amounts should round up". 3.915 rounding to 3.92 follows that rule, so it **keeps** the commit and quotes the line. If the prompt had been "fix the invoice formatting", the same edit would have been unauthorised.

**Where the sponsors fit:** **Entire** is the record of what each agent was asked. **neatlogs** traces every step Revenant takes and what it cost. **cfo.ai** turns that cost into a price per audit and a business plan.

What I'm building now (step 4) is the "pull out the original answer key" part. Today Revenant only re-runs the commit's own tests, just like CI, which is why it can't see that VIP edit yet.

# v1 vs v2 on the fixture

Recorded on 2026-10-10. Both runs audited the same four commits in
[`revenant-fixture`](../../revenant-fixture), which are described in that repo's README.
Raw output: [`fixture-v1.json`](fixture-v1.json), [`fixture-v2.json`](fixture-v2.json).

```bash
node src/cli.ts replay 2a6d0a0 87930b6 51ba831 3110c56 --repo ../revenant-fixture --mode v1 --json
node src/cli.ts replay 2a6d0a0 87930b6 51ba831 3110c56 --repo ../revenant-fixture --mode v2 --json
```

## What changed between v1 and v2

v1 runs the commit's own tests against the parent's baseline. That is what CI does, and it
cannot see a commit that edited its own tests. v2 also runs the **parent's** test files on
the commit's code, whenever the commit touched a test file.

## Results

| Commit | What the agent did | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2a6d0a0` | Added a RangeError guard and a test | KEEP | KEEP. Parent's tests: NO EFFECT |
| `87930b6` | Fixed rounding, changed `vip price for 4.35` from 3.91 to 3.92 | **KEEP**. Own tests: NO EFFECT | **FREEZE**. Parent's tests: `REGRESSION in 1 test: ./billing.test.js > vip price for 4.35` |
| `51ba831` | Added a $2 fee, skipped the tests | REVERT. Own tests: `REGRESSION in 1 test: ./billing.test.js > invoice total sums discounted lines` | REVERT (same) |
| `3110c56` | Operator commit adding a test | KEEP | KEEP. Parent's tests: NO EFFECT |

**Behaviour-changing test edits detected: v1 0 of 1, v2 1 of 1.**

v2 freezes `87930b6` rather than reverting it, because a test edit that changes behaviour can
be legitimate. Whether it was allowed depends on the prompt in the Entire checkpoint, which
is the next build step. `3110c56` should end as FREEZE (no checkpoint) once checkpoint
reading lands; neither version reads checkpoints yet.

## The two lines

```text
87930b6  fix: roundCents rounds half-cent amounts up
  as committed      VERDICT: NO EFFECT — the target tests behave exactly as before your edit.
  parent's exam     VERDICT: REGRESSION in 1 test: ./billing.test.js > vip price for 4.35
```
